steps.working: The products of complete combustion are carbon dioxide and water: CO₂ and H₂O.
steps.decision: The question asked for formulae, so write formulae. Summer 2025's report records names given instead, which were not credited.

options: Because the question asked for formulae, and a name is a different kind of answer
Because names are always wrong in chemistry
Because CO₂ is shorter to write
whyMenu.explain: Names are perfectly good chemistry; they are just not what this question asked for. Read the command.

steps.working: CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O: one carbon needs one CO₂, and four hydrogens need two H₂O.
steps.decision: Carbons first, then hydrogens. Neither of those counts can change later, which is why oxygen is left to last.

steps.working: Oxygen atoms on the right: 2 + 2 = 4, so 2 molecules of O₂. The equation is CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.
steps.decision: Balance oxygen last because it appears in both products. Counting one O₂ for the single carbon gives 1 and leaves the water unbalanced.

steps.working: Test: bubble the gas through limewater.
steps.decision: Say what you do to the gas. 'Use limewater' without bubbling the gas through it was recorded as an incomplete answer.

steps.working: Result: the colourless limewater turns milky.
steps.decision: Give both states of the solution. 'Clear' is refused every year in place of colourless.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: (a) CO₂ and H₂O. (b) CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. (c) Bubble the gas through limewater: the colourless solution turns milky.

steps.working: Starved of air means incomplete combustion: the products are carbon monoxide and water, and sometimes carbon as soot.
steps.decision: Name the gas exactly. Carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide are one word apart and mean completely different things here.

steps.working: Carbon monoxide is toxic: it combines with haemoglobin in the blood.
steps.decision: Haemoglobin is the marking word. 'It is poisonous' on its own says nothing about how.

steps.working: So the blood can carry less oxygen round the body.
steps.decision: Finish the chain. The mark is for the consequence, not just the binding.

steps.working: Another pollutant: sulfur dioxide, from sulfur impurities in the fuel.
steps.decision: Say where it comes from. Sulfur is an impurity in the fuel, not part of the hydrocarbon.

steps.working: It causes acid rain, which damages buildings, destroys vegetation and kills fish.
steps.decision: Give an effect from the specification's own list rather than a general 'it is bad for the environment'.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: (a) Carbon monoxide and water, with carbon (soot) as well. (b) Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin in the blood, so the blood can carry less oxygen. (c) Sulfur dioxide, from sulfur impurities in the fuel, causes acid rain, which damages buildings, destroys vegetation and kills fish.

items.stem: Which two elements does a hydrocarbon contain?
items.skill: Prerequisite from c2-homologous-series-alkanes; you are not expected to have met combustion yet

options.feedback: Only those two, which is why burning one can only give carbon compounds and water.
That is water. The oxygen in combustion comes from the air, not from the fuel.
That is carbon dioxide, which is a product. The fuel is hydrogen and carbon.

items.stem: In a balanced equation, what must be true?

options.text: there are the same number of each kind of atom on both sides
options.feedback: Atoms are conserved. Every combustion equation in this lesson is balanced by counting them.

options.text: there are the same number of molecules on both sides
options.feedback: Molecules can change in number; atoms cannot. CH₄ + 2O₂ has three molecules and gives three, but that is a coincidence.

options.text: the formulae may be changed to make it balance
options.feedback: Never. Only the big numbers in front may change; a formula is fixed by the chemistry.

items.stem: What does limewater do when carbon dioxide is bubbled through it?

options.feedback: Colourless to milky. Both halves of that are marked in this topic.
White to blue is anhydrous copper(II) sulfate testing for water, which is the other test here.
Fizzing is what an acid does to a carbonate. Limewater goes milky.

items.stem: A question asks for the formulae of the two substances made when methane burns completely. Which answer earns both marks?
items.skill: Give formulae when formulae are asked for

options.feedback: Formulae were asked for, and these are they.
Right chemistry, wrong form: the question asked for formulae, and Summer 2025 records names earning nothing here.
Carbon monoxide comes from incomplete combustion. With plenty of oxygen the carbon ends up as CO₂.
The hydrogen leaves as water, not as hydrogen gas: it has just reacted with oxygen.

items.stem: What is produced when a hydrocarbon burns in a limited supply of oxygen?
items.skill: Recall the products of incomplete combustion

options.text: carbon monoxide and water, and sometimes carbon
options.feedback: All three are on the specification, and the soot is the one you can see.
That is complete combustion. A limited supply cannot give every carbon the two oxygens it needs.
The hydrogen still ends up as water; what changes is what happens to the carbon.
Sulfur dioxide comes from sulfur impurities in the fuel, not from the hydrocarbon itself.

items.skill: Explain the toxicity of carbon monoxide

options.text: it combines with haemoglobin, reducing the blood's capacity to carry oxygen
options.feedback: Haemoglobin and the reduced oxygen capacity are the two halves the scheme wants.

options.text: it is an acid gas that burns the lungs
options.feedback: That is closer to sulfur dioxide. Carbon monoxide works on the blood, not by being acidic.
It can burn, but that is not why it kills people in their homes. It stops the blood carrying oxygen.

options.text: it blocks the airways with soot
options.feedback: Soot is the solid particles; carbon monoxide is a colourless, odourless gas that you cannot feel at all.

items.stem: Which pollutant causes acid rain, and where does it come from?
items.skill: Match a pollutant to its effect

options.text: sulfur dioxide, from sulfur impurities in the fuel
options.feedback: The sulfur is an impurity, not part of the hydrocarbon, which is why removing it helps.
Carbon dioxide's problem on this specification is the greenhouse effect. Acid rain is sulfur dioxide's.
Carbon monoxide is toxic to people. It is not what the specification blames for acid rain.
Soot damages lungs and blackens buildings, but acid rain comes from sulfur dioxide.

items.stem: What does carbon dioxide from burning fuels cause?

options.text: the greenhouse effect, leading to climate change and sea-level rise
options.feedback: Greenhouse effect first, then a consequence from the specification's list.
Acid rain is sulfur dioxide's doing. Carbon dioxide's is the greenhouse effect.

options.text: a hole in the ozone layer
options.feedback: The ozone layer is a separate story and not on this specification. Carbon dioxide traps heat instead.
That is soot. Carbon dioxide is a gas that traps heat, not a particle.

items.stem: Balance the complete combustion of methane: CH₄ + ___ O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.

options.feedback: The products hold four oxygen atoms and each O₂ brings two, so two molecules.
That gives one O₂ for the single carbon and forgets the two waters, which need oxygen too.
That is the number of oxygen ATOMS the products hold. Each O₂ molecule supplies two of them, so halve it.
Three O₂ would put six oxygen atoms in, and the products can only take four.

parts.stem:
A gas burner can be run with its air hole open or closed.
Describe what is produced in each case, and explain how the products of burning fuels pollute the atmosphere.
This question also assesses the quality of your written communication, including your use of specialist scientific terms.

bands.descriptor: Five or six of the indicative points, described in detail, with specialist chemical terms used widely and accurately; organised with clarity; spelling, punctuation and grammar good enough that the meaning is clear throughout.
Three or four of the indicative points; some specialist chemical vocabulary; organised with some clarity; spelling, punctuation and grammar competent enough for the meaning to be clear.
One or two of the indicative points; little specialist vocabulary; organisation may lack clarity; spelling, punctuation and grammar may leave the intended meaning unclear.

indicativeContent.point: With the air hole open there is plenty of oxygen, so combustion is complete.
Complete combustion gives carbon dioxide and water.
With the air hole closed the oxygen supply is limited, so combustion is incomplete.
Incomplete combustion gives carbon monoxide and water, and sometimes carbon as soot.
Carbon dioxide adds to the greenhouse effect, causing climate change, sea-level rise and flooding.
Carbon monoxide is toxic because it combines with haemoglobin, so the blood can carry less oxygen; soot damages the lungs.
Sulfur impurities in the fuel give sulfur dioxide, which causes acid rain that damages buildings, destroys vegetation and kills fish.

scheme.for: a banded answer covering both burns and all three pollution routes: plenty of oxygen giving carbon dioxide and water, limited oxygen giving carbon monoxide, water and soot, and then the greenhouse effect, the toxicity of carbon monoxide with soot damaging lungs, and sulfur dioxide causing acid rain
scheme.examinerNote: A point contradicted elsewhere in the answer is not counted. Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement.

hints: Two burns, then three pollutants.
Each pollutant needs an effect, not just a name.
parts.workedSolution: With the air hole open the burner gets plenty of oxygen, so the fuel burns completely and gives carbon dioxide and water. With the air hole closed the oxygen supply is limited, so combustion is incomplete: the products are carbon monoxide and water, and often carbon as soot. All three pollute. Carbon dioxide adds to the greenhouse effect, which causes climate change, sea-level rise and flooding. Carbon monoxide is toxic because it combines with haemoglobin in the blood and reduces its capacity to carry oxygen, and soot particles damage the lungs. Sulfur impurities in the fuel burn to give sulfur dioxide, which causes acid rain, damaging buildings, destroying vegetation and killing fish.

parts.workedSolution: Three carbons give 3CO₂; eight hydrogens give 4H₂O. The products hold 3 × 2 + 4 = 10 oxygen atoms, which is 5O₂: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O.

findTheMistake.stem:
Seán is asked: 'Methane burns completely. Give the formula of each product [2], and name the pollutant that causes acid rain [1].'
His answer:
studentWorking: The products are carbon dioxide and water.
Acid rain is caused by sulfur dioxide, from sulfur impurities in the fuel.
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The acid-rain line is right and complete. The first line names the products where the question asked for formulae, so it earns nothing: the answer wanted is CO2 and H2O. Summer 2025's report records this exact substitution.
correction: The products are CO2 and H2O.
findTheMistake.feedback: One of the three marks. The chemistry in the first line is right, which makes it a painful loss: the command word asked for formulae, so give formulae. Read the noun in the question — name, formula or equation — before you write.

findTheMistake.stem:
Niamh is asked: 'Describe the test for water and give the result. [2]'
Her answer:
studentWorking: Add anhydrous copper(II) sulfate to the liquid.
It turns from blue to white.
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 2 runs the colour change backwards. Anhydrous copper(II) sulfate is a white powder, and water turns it blue; blue to white is what you see when blue crystals are heated. Line 1 is right.
correction: It turns from white to blue.
findTheMistake.feedback: One mark of the two: the reagent stands. In 2024 blue to white earned no credit, so write the colour it starts first: white, then blue.

prompts.prompt: Methane burns completely in oxygen. Write the word equation and the balanced symbol equation.
prompts.answer: methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water; CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O.

prompts.prompt: What is produced when a hydrocarbon burns in a limited supply of oxygen?
prompts.answer: Carbon monoxide and water, and sometimes carbon, seen as soot.

prompts.prompt: Give the test and the full result for carbon dioxide.
prompts.answer: Bubble the gas through limewater: the colourless solution turns milky. Colourless, not clear.

prompts.prompt: Give the test and the full result for water.
prompts.answer: Add anhydrous copper(II) sulfate: it turns from white to blue.
It combines with haemoglobin in the blood, so the blood can carry less oxygen.

prompts.prompt: What does carbon dioxide from burning fuels cause, and what does that lead to?
prompts.answer: The greenhouse effect, which causes climate change, sea-level rise and flooding.

prompts.prompt: Where does the sulfur dioxide from a power station come from, and what does it cause?
prompts.answer: From sulfur impurities in the fuel. It causes acid rain, which damages buildings, destroys vegetation and kills fish.

prompts.prompt: In what order do you balance a combustion equation, and why?
prompts.answer: Carbons first, then hydrogens, then oxygen last, because oxygen appears in both products so its count is only fixed once they are.

prompts.prompt: Which gas from sulfur impurities in fuels causes acid rain?
Which molecule in the blood does carbon monoxide combine with?

findings.asked: Write methane's two complete-combustion products as formulae, and identify the toxic gas made when it burns short of oxygen.
findings.wentWrong: The formulae were poorly answered: many wrote the names, which earned nothing. Almost every candidate identified carbon monoxide.
findings.rule: Formulae asked, formulae given: CO2 and H2O.

findings.asked: Formulae for the complete-combustion products, then a balanced equation for methane burning short of oxygen.
findings.wentWrong: The formulae were widely known. Some struggled with the incomplete-combustion equation, though most earned marks for the formulae of the reactants or the products.
findings.rule: Formulae first, then carbons, hydrogens and oxygen last; a half in front of O2 is accepted.

findings.asked: The test for carbon dioxide within a six-mark answer, the colour anhydrous copper(II) sulfate turns with water, and the black solid from the incomplete combustion of ethane.
findings.wentWrong: Marks were lost when answers left out that the gas is bubbled through and that the limewater starts colourless, and clear was refused for colourless. Only white to blue was accepted for copper(II) sulfate. Very few named soot or carbon; coal, tar and charcoal were common.
findings.rule: Bubble the gas through limewater: colourless to milky. Anhydrous copper(II) sulfate: white to blue. The black solid is carbon, called soot.

findings.asked: Draw butane, write the word equation for its complete combustion, and name the toxic gas from its incomplete combustion.
findings.wentWrong: Only a few wrote the correct word equation for burning butane; naming the toxic gas was very well answered.

insight.ruleToRemember: Plenty of oxygen gives carbon dioxide and water; too little gives carbon monoxide, water and sometimes soot. Balance carbons, then hydrogens, then oxygen last. Water turns anhydrous copper(II) sulfate from white to blue; carbon dioxide turns colourless limewater milky. Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin; carbon dioxide drives the greenhouse effect; sulfur dioxide gives acid rain.
insight.aStarSignal: Balancing an incomplete-combustion equation with a half or a doubled set of numbers, and giving every colour change in full.
